tasks.short: Agree event objectives, requirements and success measures with the customer.

steps.what: Read the enquiry and previous event records before discovery.
Explore objectives, audience, constraints and competing priorities with the customer.
Write the event brief and list unresolved requirements.

loop.input: Discovery record, approved brief template and retrieved event records.
loop.output: Draft event brief with source references and explicit open questions.
loop.check: Check required fields and source references; planner verifies objectives, constraints and omitted disagreements.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unresolved or unsupported statements return to the planner.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template handles structure, but turning conversational notes into a faithful brief requires language interpretation.

steps.what: Resolve open questions and agree the brief with the customer.
Save the agreed brief and update the event record.

tasks.design: An integration gathers authorised records from the {CRM} and {DOCS} into a discovery pack. A bounded drafting loop prepares the brief from the planner's notes; after customer agreement, a configured flow versions it in {DOCS} and updates the {PROJECT} event baseline.
tasks.previous_blocker: Objectives emerge through conversation, while notes and past commitments sit in separate records. Templates alone cannot resolve ambiguous priorities.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing retrieval and workflow features can handle preparation and filing. AI coding reduces the effort of connecting them, and bounded drafting can turn notes into a reviewable brief.
tasks.still_hard: Customers may disagree internally, withhold constraints or change their objectives. Recording conversations also requires an appropriate GDPR basis and clear retention arrangements.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust, expose conflicting expectations and help the customer choose what the event should achieve.

ambition.what: Event success-measure workshop before supplier commitments.

tasks.altitude: The planner spends less time assembling records and rewriting notes, with more preparation for difficult discovery conversations. Decision rights remain unchanged; the customer approves scope and priorities.

reach.role: Market Research Analysts and Marketing Specialists
reach.task: Turn event objectives into an attendee research plan.
reach.learn: Question design, sampling limits and how to distinguish attendance from useful outcomes.

evidence.claim: Structured intake, record retrieval and versioned briefs can reduce preparation and filing work.
Bounded drafting can assist with conversational notes, but customer alignment remains human work.

assumptions: The customer may be an internal event sponsor or an external client.
The planner writes discovery notes; automatic recording is optional.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
Conversation remains the largest time component, consistent with the supplied priors.
Access estimates include privacy review and employee consultation where national rules require it.
unknowns: Where previous event records and customer commitments are stored.
Who can approve the event brief and subsequent scope changes.
Whether customer agreements permit the proposed processing of discovery notes.
research_questions: Which brief fields most often change after initial agreement?
How reliably does drafting preserve disagreements and distinguish decisions from suggestions?
new_work: Review generated briefs against discovery notes.
Maintain brief templates and retrieval permissions.
Resolve missing records and prevent outdated commitments entering new briefs.

tasks.short: Check event invoices against agreed charges and approve valid bills for payment.

steps.what: Collect invoices, orders, contracts and evidence of delivered services.
Read invoice lines and identify charges, quantities, taxes and deposits.

loop.input: Document invoices that lack usable structured invoice data.
loop.output: Invoice fields and lines with page references and uncertainty flags.
loop.check: Validate required fields, totals, tax arithmetic and duplicates; route uncertain or inconsistent fields for review.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per invoice; failure returns to manual entry.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured invoices use deterministic parsing; variable document layouts and charge descriptions need bounded extraction.

steps.what: Compare charges with orders, rates, delivered quantities and prior payments.
Resolve disputed extras and missing delivery evidence with the supplier.
Approve valid charges within delegated spending authority.
Record approval and make the invoice available for the payment process.

tasks.design: Configure matching and approval routing in the {ERP}, linking orders from {PROCUREMENT} and delivery evidence from {DOCS}. A bounded extraction loop handles document invoices, while deterministic checks produce an exception pack for the planner and an approval view for the budget holder. Approved payables enter the finance team's payment workflow with an audit trail.
tasks.previous_blocker: Invoices describe event extras inconsistently, and delivery evidence often sits outside the finance records. Missing order references force manual investigation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing matching features cover rates, quantities, deposits and duplicates. Small integrations and bounded document extraction make the supporting evidence easier to assemble.
tasks.still_hard: Disputed service quality, verbal changes, cancellations and unusual tax treatment need accountable review. Poor purchasing records still limit automatic matching.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether services were acceptable and settle disputed charges without damaging supplier relationships.

ambition.what: Review committed event cost against budget after each accepted service change.

tasks.altitude: The planner reviews commercial exceptions instead of checking every line. Spending authority remains with the delegated budget holder, and payment release remains a finance decision.

reach.task: Compare event cost with campaign outcomes when allocating the next budget.
reach.learn: Accruals, committed spend and the limits of event attribution.

evidence.claim: Transporeon checks freight invoices against agreed rates; this supports the matching pattern, not event-specific results.
Configured order matching and approval routing can handle routine invoice checks when reliable purchasing records exist.
Document extraction requires validation before its fields support financial approval.

assumptions: The planner approves only within delegated authority; larger bills go to a separate budget holder.
The estimates cover planner, budget-holder and finance handling within this task.
The existing {ERP} supports matching tolerances and approval routing.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
The document and spreadsheet shares reflect manual reconciliation, while approval already uses the {ERP}.
unknowns: The proportion of invoices with structured data and valid order references.
The available matching features and interfaces in the {ERP}.
Approval limits, segregation requirements and permitted matching tolerances.
Where deposits, credit notes and service acceptance records are recorded.
research_questions: Which discrepancies explain most investigation time?
Can the matching rules reliably distinguish deposits, final balances and duplicate charges?
How often do extraction errors escape arithmetic and reference checks?
new_work: Review uncertain invoice fields and unmatched charges.
Maintain matching tolerances and approval delegations.
Monitor duplicate detection and reconcile failed integrations.
Sample matched invoices to detect rule drift.

tasks.short: Coordinate suppliers, participant needs and service readiness for an event.

steps.what: Translate the agreed brief into a service plan with owners and deadlines.
Collect participant numbers, travel details and accommodation or accessibility needs.
Request supplier availability, prices and service constraints.
Combine offers and equipment reservations into a timed service schedule.

loop.input: Supplier replies and attachments containing prices, capacities, deadlines and service constraints.
loop.output: Source-linked service offer fields for deterministic scheduling and conflict checks.
loop.check: Validate dates, currencies, capacities and required fields; planner checks uncertain terms before scheduling.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction attempt per reply; ambiguity becomes a service conflict for human resolution.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured offers bypass the loop, but free-text supplier terms cannot reliably be mapped with fixed field rules.

steps.what: Resolve service conflicts, substitutions and sensitive requirements with relevant people.
Approve service orders and send authorised requirements to suppliers.
Check service readiness with the venue and record outstanding problems.

tasks.design: A service register in the {PROJECT} connects structured participant intake in the {WORKFLOW}, supplier requests through {EMAIL}, and approved orders in {PROCUREMENT}. Deterministic templates build schedules, check capacities and flag missing confirmations; a bounded loop extracts terms from free-text replies. Restricted views share only necessary participant requirements, while the planner approves commitments and resolves conflicts.
tasks.previous_blocker: Service dependencies cross suppliers, participant messages and equipment bookings. Repeated copying hides which version and commitment are current.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured forms, shared records and deterministic dependency checks cover much of the coordination. AI coding reduces integration effort, and bounded extraction handles remaining supplier documents.
tasks.still_hard: Supplier disruption and conflicting participant needs require negotiation. Accessibility or dietary details can reveal special-category data, requiring a GDPR lawful basis, an applicable special-category condition and restricted sharing.
tasks.human_edge: Make workable trade-offs across suppliers and participants, especially when service failure affects dignity, access or safety.

ambition.what: Pre-event accessibility readiness review with affected participants.

tasks.altitude: The planner works from a current service schedule and spends more time resolving dependencies before they become urgent. They can coordinate recovery options within existing authority; additional spending still needs delegated approval.

reach.task: Compare travel, catering and accommodation options for an event.
reach.learn: Activity data, emissions boundaries and how to express uncertainty in supplier estimates.

evidence.claim: Shared service records, structured intake and deterministic dependency checks can reduce event coordination work.
Free-text supplier replies can support bounded extraction with source checks and human exception handling.
Special-category participant data needs an applicable GDPR condition in addition to a lawful basis.

assumptions: This task coordinates service dependencies; equipment reservations are handled in task 13-1121.00:1215.
Structured intake includes an assisted route for participants who cannot use the form.
Supplier requests expose operational requirements only, rather than unnecessary diagnoses or personal details.
The budget holder may be the planner where delegated authority permits.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
Consultation and access estimates include employee-data review where national rules apply.
unknowns: Which suppliers accept structured requests and provide usable confirmations.
Who can access participant needs and authorise their sharing.
Which GDPR bases, special-category conditions and retention periods apply.
Which service changes the planner may approve without escalation.
Whether employee consultation is required under applicable national rules.
research_questions: Which dependencies most often cause late service changes?
Can participant requirements be translated into operational instructions without retaining sensitive explanations?
How often do supplier replies omit a condition that affects the schedule?
new_work: Review extracted supplier constraints and schedule conflicts.
Maintain service templates, lead times and escalation contacts.
Handle incomplete participant submissions through the assisted route.
Review sensitive-data access and delete details after their retention period.
Monitor overdue confirmations and failed supplier connections.

tasks.short: Reserve event equipment and transport, coordinate delivery, and verify readiness.

steps.what: Specify equipment, transport capacity and technical requirements for the event.
Check supplier availability, compatibility, prices and booking conditions.

loop.input: Availability replies, equipment specifications and supplier booking conditions.
loop.output: Source-linked availability, prices, compatibility claims and expiry times.
loop.check: Check identifiers, dates and quantities; require technical review of ambiguous compatibility and mark availability as unreserved.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per reply; missing or conflicting facts go to the planner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Portal data uses deterministic mapping, but many suppliers describe substitutions and conditions in free text.

steps.what: Select an available option and approve the reservation.
Prepare delivery, setup, collection and fallback instructions for the venue.
Test equipment and verify transport, setup and fallback arrangements.
Confirm readiness after technical issues are resolved or escalated.

tasks.design: A reservation register in the {PROJECT} links approved equipment specifications in {DOCS} with bookings in {PROCUREMENT} and confirmations from the {PARTNER_PORTAL} or {EMAIL}. Deterministic checks flag date clashes, missing quantities and expiring offers, while a bounded loop extracts free-text supplier conditions. Approved reservations generate logistics plans, and readiness updates require a completed technical check and planner approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier availability is temporary, specifications vary, and technical knowledge often lives with individuals. Booking confirmations and venue instructions are copied between separate records.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured reservation records and document templates cover routine paperwork. Small integrations expose booking changes, while bounded extraction makes unstructured confirmations usable.
tasks.still_hard: A stated specification cannot prove that equipment works in the room. Physical testing, substitutions and urgent supplier recovery still need experienced people.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise practical incompatibilities, test the actual setup and choose a safe, credible fallback under time pressure.

ambition.what: Pre-event technical rehearsal for events with remote speakers.

tasks.altitude: The planner spends less time chasing confirmations and copying logistics details, leaving more time for rehearsals and fallback planning. Booking and readiness authority remain within existing delegations.

reach.task: Check display artwork against the booked screens and print surfaces.
reach.learn: Aspect ratios, resolution, viewing distance and technical handoff specifications.

evidence.claim: Reservation records, conflict checks and logistics templates can reduce equipment booking administration.
Availability information needs a confirmed reservation before it can be treated as a booking.
Physical testing remains necessary to establish readiness of the actual event setup.

assumptions: The technical lead may be a venue or supplier specialist.
The equipment reservation record feeds the broader service schedule in task 13-1121.00:1214.
Technical specification work uses structured checklists, but final equipment suitability remains a human judgement.
The budget holder may be the planner where delegated authority permits.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
Build ranges assume a limited initial supplier set; broad portal coverage would take longer.
unknowns: Which suppliers provide reservation interfaces or only email confirmations.
Whether internal equipment has a reliable availability register.
Who signs off compatibility, safety and event readiness.
Which cancellation terms and spending limits apply.
Whether transport bookings contain personal data requiring additional access controls.
research_questions: Which compatibility checks can be expressed as reliable rules?
How quickly does supplier availability become stale?
Which past failures would a rehearsal detect before event day?
new_work: Review extracted booking conditions and proposed substitutions.
Maintain equipment identifiers, compatibility rules and logistics templates.
Resolve stale availability and failed confirmation updates.
Keep technical test evidence and escalation contacts current.

role.altitude: The planner's week shifts from copying, chasing and routine checking toward discovery, commercial exceptions and readiness rehearsals. Customers, budget holders and technical specialists retain their approval rights; the planner gains earlier visibility of risks.
reach: Connect event objectives to attendee research with market research specialists.
Support marketing managers with reconciled event costs and clearly defined outcomes.
Compare service options with sustainability specialists.
Improve technical handoffs with graphic designers.
skills_to_grow: Discovery interviewing and measurable event objectives.
Technical specifications, rehearsals and fallback planning.
GDPR data minimisation and restricted handling of participant needs.
Checking generated documents and maintaining deterministic workflow rules.
role.ambitious_version: Offer an event readiness service combining agreed success measures, accessibility review, technical rehearsal and current committed costs before delivery.
